source_name: UNDP Montenegro — FinTech regulatory framework assessment (regional/donor analysis)
why_relevant: Donor-funded assessments name incumbent providers, market structure and cross-border dependencies that vendors do not publish; they also list stakeholders consulted, which functions as an actor map for the ME fintech/banking supply side.

source_name: Komisija za zaštitu prava u postupcima javnih nabavki Crne Gore — baza rješenja
why_relevant: Searchable database of procurement-appeal decisions. Decisions name the contracting authority (naručilac), the appellant (žalilac), competing bidders, the procurement subject and often the exact equipment/software offered — the single best public window into contested IT/ATM/card-system tenders in Montenegro and into who actually bid against whom.

source_name: MANS institutional profile of the Procurement Rights Protection Commission
why_relevant: NGO watchdog page describing the Commission's mandate, caseload statistics and reporting; useful as a pointer to annual reports, FOI (slobodan pristup informacijama) routes and to MANS' own procurement investigations that often name suppliers.

source_name: Državna komisija za kontrolu postupaka javnih nabavki — izvještaj o radu (gov.me document store)
why_relevant: Annual work reports aggregate appeal statistics and frequently cite illustrative cases with contracting authority and subject matter; helps size how many IT/banking-equipment tenders are contested and identify serial appellants (often the losing vendor).

source_name: Zavod za zapošljavanje Crne Gore — slobodna radna mjesta (SRM) vacancy database
why_relevant: The statutory national vacancy register: every employer, including banks, publishes openings here. Job texts for 'administrator', 'IT' and 'operacije' roles routinely name the platform the bank runs. Filterable by occupation category, municipality and archive status, with 126+ pages of history — i.e. a longitudinal record of incumbency signals.

source_name: CKB Banka careers portal (TalentLyft)
why_relevant: OTP-owned CKB posts its own openings with an explicit 'IT i operacije' department filter. Bank-run ATS pages carry the fullest technical requirement text (named core/card/channel platforms) before it is trimmed for aggregators.

source_name: Bankar.me — Oglasi za posao (banking job-ads section)
why_relevant: Sector-specific Montenegrin banking portal that republishes bank job ads (CBCG, Prva banka, Erste, Ziraat, NLB and others) with full text. Acts both as an indirect incumbency signal and as a pointer to which banks are staffing up which functions; also carries vendor/project news.

source_name: Posao.crna.gora.me — Montenegro job portal (IT/banking categories)
why_relevant: Commercial job board with per-position permalinks (e.g. IT mrežni administrator) and deep pagination archives; mirrors ZZZCG plus direct employer ads. Technology names in requirement lists are the weak signal of interest.

source_name: Zaposli.ME — IT job category
why_relevant: Described in results as among the most-visited ME employment sites; its IT category is where bank and bank-vendor engineering roles (and vendor subcontractors hiring for a named bank project) surface.

source_name: Prekoveze.me — IT job listings
why_relevant: Secondary ME job board with an IT vertical; useful for redundancy since smaller vendors and integrators sometimes post only here.

source_name: MojTrg.me — Posao / Informacione tehnologije classifieds
why_relevant: Classifieds board IT-jobs section; catches informal/contractor postings (e.g. ATM field service, POS technician) that reveal who services which bank's estate.

source_name: CKB Bank LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: Bank LinkedIn pages carry go-live announcements, digital-channel launches, hiring posts and photos from vendor workshops; employee job titles on the page reveal which platforms the bank staffs for. Highest-value weak signal for who supplies CKB/OTP in Montenegro.

source_name: Asseco SEE (ASEE) news & references — Montenegro client announcements
why_relevant: Vendor's own newsroom explicitly names ME clients and the deployed product (e.g. ASEBA JiMBa mobile banking at NLB Montenegro). Vendor-tags-client announcements are the cleanest incumbency proof after appeal decisions; the same newsroom is mirrored by ASEE LinkedIn posts.

source_name: Temenos success stories — NLB group
why_relevant: Group-level vendor case study covering NLB across SEE including Montenegro; establishes group-standard platform decisions that cascade to the ME subsidiary even when the ME entity is never named directly.

source_name: Portal pravosuđa Crne Gore — Privredni sud Crne Gore (decisions/announcements)
why_relevant: The Commercial Court hears contract disputes between banks and their IT suppliers. Published decisions and press items name both parties and the disputed contract, revealing supplier relationships (and failures) that never appear in marketing.

source_name: PRAVOSUDJE.me — judiciary portal (cross-court decision search)
why_relevant: Umbrella judiciary portal linking all Montenegrin courts' decision pages; the entry point for locating the Administrative Court (Upravni sud) rulings that review procurement-commission decisions — the appeal-of-the-appeal layer.

source_name: CRPS — Centralni registar privrednih subjekata (business register search)
why_relevant: Identifies the legal entities behind vendor local subsidiaries, resellers and consortium partners named in tenders, appeals and job ads — necessary to resolve aliases/transliterations and to see who is locally registered to bid.

source_name: CBCG — Pravo na prigovor / zaštita korisnika finansijskih usluga
why_relevant: Central Bank consumer-complaint function. Complaint statistics and thematic reports expose recurring operational failures (card/ATM/e-banking outages, payment errors) that are attributable to specific systems and vendors — a classic weak signal of platform quality and change.

source_name: Odbor za vansudsko rješavanje potrošačkih sporova (Privredna komora Crne Gore)
why_relevant: Functionally independent consumer ADR body at the Chamber of Commerce, identified by CBCG as the out-of-court route for financial-services disputes. Its case summaries are a second, non-regulator stream of consumer-complaint evidence about banks' payment and card operations.

source_name: CBCG — Podaci o blokiranim pravnim licima i preduzetnicima
why_relevant: Register of blocked accounts. Screening local IT integrators and vendor subsidiaries against it is a cheap financial-distress weak signal that predicts contract failure and vendor churn at their bank clients.

source_name: Deloitte Montenegro (Deloitte d.o.o. Podgorica) - firm site, insights and audit/FA practice pages
why_relevant: Deloitte d.o.o. Podgorica (office opened 1998, Cetinjska 11) is a statutory auditor and deal/technology advisor to Montenegrin banks; its local insights, press and service pages name banking clients, transformation programmes and occasionally systems/vendors. Also the anchor for Deloitte CE regional banking studies that include ME.

source_name: Deloitte CEE/CE banking sector surveys (e.g. CEE banking sector impact surveys, Banking Barometers)
why_relevant: Regional Deloitte CEE banking surveys benchmark digital-channel investment, core-banking modernisation and cost programmes across SEE and typically include Montenegrin banks in the sample; gives comparative competitor context for vendors.

source_name: EY Montenegro (Ernst & Young Montenegro d.o.o.) and EY SEE banking publications
why_relevant: EY Montenegro is a registered audit firm in the ICAM register and audits/advises Montenegrin banks; EY's global and SEE banking transformation and EY-IIF risk surveys set the benchmark frame that local banks cite when justifying digital investment.

source_name: PricewaterhouseCoopers d.o.o. Montenegro (PwC) - local audit/advisory entity
why_relevant: PwC is listed in the Montenegrin register of audit firms and audits/advises banks; PwC SEE publications (banking in CEE, digital banking surveys) and its ME entity's statutory audit engagements are a route to identifying which banks are running modernisation programmes.

source_name: KPMG in Montenegro / KPMG Adriatic banking publications
why_relevant: KPMG audits several regional bank groups with Montenegrin subsidiaries and publishes Adriatic/SEE banking analyses; auditor identity plus advisory publications reveal which institutions are in transformation and who advises them.

source_name: Institut sertifikovanih računovođa Crne Gore (ICAM) - register of audit firms and licensed auditors
why_relevant: Authoritative actor map of the ~37 audit firms licensed in Montenegro (Deloitte DOO, Ernst & Young Montenegro DOO, PricewaterhouseCoopers DOO, BDO, Crowe MNE, HLB Mont Audit, TPA, Baker-Tilly-type mid-tier, etc.). Anchors which advisers can sign bank audits and therefore who sits inside bank IT/controls reviews.

source_name: CBCG - Finansijski izvještaji banaka (audited bank financial statements with independent auditor reports)
why_relevant: Central repository of every Montenegrin bank's audited annual and quarterly statements (CKB/OTP, Hipotekarna, Podgorička banka, Prva banka, Erste, NLB, Adriatic, Universal Capital, Ziraat, Lovćen, Addiko where applicable). Auditor identity, intangible-asset/software capex, IT outsourcing notes and 'ulaganja u informacione sisteme' lines are the highest-signal indirect evidence of digital-channel and core-banking investment.
